why: Each '?' choice only affects its neighbours, so a DP over the string with state 'last character is 0 or 1' captures everything: dp[i][c] = fewest mismatches in the prefix ending at i with character c.
hints: The cost only involves adjacent pairs. What is the only thing about the prefix you need to remember when deciding position i?
Keep two values: best inefficiency so far if position i is '0', and if it is '1'. A fixed character forbids one of them; '?' allows both.
new0 = min(dp0, dp1 + 1) if position i can be '0' (else infinity), symmetric for new1. Answer min(dp0, dp1). O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: Leading '?' have no left neighbour: filling them with a fixed '0' can add a needless mismatch ("??1" should become "111"). The DP, which tries both characters, avoids this.
A string of only '?' has inefficiency 0.
Initialise the forbidden state at position 0 to infinity, not 0.
